memory_candidates.content: jq's join() degrades gracefully on an array of strings but ERRORS on an array of objects ("string (...) and object (...) cannot be added", exit 5), with no partial output. Wrapping such a substitution in 2>/dev/null silently converts that error into an empty command-substitution result, which then threads through a `[ -z "$x" ] && x=fallback` guard indistinguishably from a genuinely empty input -- turning a type-mismatch bug into an invisible one that looks like routine degradation. Before trusting a jq pipeline's `2>/dev/null` silence as "nothing to report", re-run the same expression without the redirect against a schema instance that actually contains the object shape the pipeline is meant to handle.

When adding a new synthetic numeric fixture identifier (a "candidate #N" directory/number) to a large test file with hundreds of existing fixtures, grep the whole file for that number before use (e.g. `grep -n '<N>_candidate\|#<N>'`). A collision with an existing fixture using the same number will not fail the test suite -- setup_sandbox's per-fixture `rm -rf $WORKDIR` means each fixture runs in isolation regardless -- so nothing mechanical catches the duplicate; only a manual pre-check does, and the cost of skipping it is a confusing double-use of the same identifier for future readers grepping by number.
